title: Derive a webhook decoder's payload types from a sealed hierarchy

blocks.text: The parcel service receives tracking webhooks from its carriers. Each payload carries a `"type"` field, and the decoder looks that name up in a map to find the record class to decode into. The map was written by hand, and when the carriers' `Damaged` events were split into `Crushed` and `Soaked`, nobody updated it: for two days every damage report was rejected as an unknown type.

The payload types already form sealed hierarchies of records, so the decoder should build the map from the hierarchy at startup. `of(...)` and `register(...)` are written. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PayloadTypes.java`:

items: `collect(...)`: add every record class a value of the given type can be.

blocks.text: When you're done, `of(...)` returns every payload record of a hierarchy however it is nested, and nothing else. A map it can't make complete is worse than none, so for such a type `of(...)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` instead of returning. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: for a sealed interface whose subtypes are all records, every record is in the map under its lower-case simple name
records under a sealed sub-interface, two levels down, are in the map, and the sub-interfaces themselves are not
an interface that isn't sealed is refused with IllegalArgumentException, since its implementations can't be listed

origin.section: At Run Time, getPermittedSubclasses() Lists the Direct Subtypes Only

concepts: getPermittedSubclasses() returns only the direct subtypes, so code that needs every concrete type walks down through each sealed subtype, and it returns null for a type that isn't sealed.
